summary: Defines the EDIINT-Features header field, which lets EDIINT applications (AS1, AS2, AS3) announce optional features they support. This helps avoid problems when a partner does not support a feature. It is informational.

eli5.summary: Businesses exchange orders and invoices over the internet. This adds a header where each side lists the extras it can do, so nobody tries something their partner cannot handle.

subtitle: A header field for announcing optional features in EDIINT business messaging.

tldr.problem: EDIINT systems (AS1, AS2, AS3) support optional features that not all implementations have. When a sender uses a feature the receiver does not support, messages fail silently or cause errors.
tldr.mechanism: Add an EDIINT-Features header field that lists the capabilities each side supports. Trading partners can then choose only features the other side has announced.
tldr.outcome: Implementations can negotiate feature support without out-of-band communication, avoiding incompatibility problems.

today: RFC 6017 remains Informational. It is used by EDIINT systems that need to advertise support for optional features. The header is registered with IANA as a provisional header for HTTP and email.

sections.title: EDIINT Messaging Features
sections.content:
EDIINT (Electronic Data Interchange - Internet Integration) includes three protocols: AS1 (email), AS2 (HTTP), and AS3 (FTP). These protocols started as basic secure transport, but newer features have been added: compression, new encryption methods, and application-specific features. The problem is that not all implementations support all features.

The EDIINT-Features header field lets a sender announce which features it can use, so the receiver knows what to expect and what to send back.
sections.eli5: Businesses send orders and invoices to each other using one of three methods. Sometimes one side can do more tricks than the other, and they need to agree on what tricks to use.

sections.title: Header Syntax and Use
sections.content:
The EDIINT-Features header has the form "EDIINT-Features: feature-name, feature-name, ..." where feature names contain only alphanumeric characters and hyphens. Names are case insensitive. The header MUST appear in all messages, not just those using the features, so the recipient always knows what the sender can do.

Recipients SHOULD assume the sender can use any feature listed in the header. Features must be defined in separate RFCs so there is a published spec for each one.
sections.eli5: The header is a comma-separated list of feature names that the sender can handle.

sections.title: Connection to Version Headers
sections.content:
AS2 and AS3 already have version headers (AS2-Version and AS3-Version). An implementation that supports EDIINT-Features must set version to "1.2". Version "1.1" indicates support for compression (RFC 5402), and version "1.2" builds on "1.1", so "1.2" always includes compression support whether or not it is listed as a feature.

AS1 does not use a version header. The EDIINT-Features header is informational, so AS1, AS2, or AS3 partners that have not implemented it can safely ignore it without breaking the session.
sections.eli5: The version number tracks backwards compatibility. A system saying "1.2" promises it can do everything version 1.1 could do plus the new features.
